title: Demolition & Structural Alteration
whatItIs: Demolition, dismantling and structural alteration are high-risk work. Workers and passers-by can be hurt by falls, flying debris and the early, uncontrolled collapse of a structure.

keyFacts.text: Demolition MUST be planned and done to prevent danger, or reduce it as far as reasonably practicable.
The arrangements for demolition MUST be put in writing before the work begins.
All practicable steps MUST be taken to stop a structure collapsing if the work makes it unstable.

keyFacts: Work is done by trained demolition operatives, supervised by someone who knows the demolition sequence.
Gas, electricity, water and telecoms services are isolated or disconnected first, or clearly marked.

keyFacts.text: Demolition: the asbestos plan of work MUST say asbestos goes before other major works, so far as reasonably practicable.

visual.caption: Before the work starts (HSG150 paras 392-395; CDM 2015 reg 20)

items.title: Survey
items.text: Survey for hazardous materials and structural condition. The client provides the information.

items.title: Plan in writing
items.text: Record the arrangements in writing. Choose a method that keeps people away, eg a high-reach machine.

items.title: Exclusion zone
items.text: Barriers or hoardings keep out anyone not involved in the work.

a.label: Structural engineer
points: Used where there's doubt about stability or the method

b.label: Demolition supervisor
points: Knows the type of demolition and its hazards
Follows the method statement and sequence

onTheTest.question: When must the arrangements for a demolition job be put in writing?
options: Only if HSE asks for them
onTheTest.why: CDM 2015 reg 20(2): the arrangements for demolition or dismantling must be recorded in writing before the work begins.

onTheTest.question: Why is an exclusion zone set up around demolition work?
options: To keep people not involved away from falling material
To give plant somewhere to park
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 395: keep anyone not involved away with an exclusion zone marked by barriers or hoardings. Don't let materials fall where people work or pass.

traps: Follow the set sequence: working out of order can cause an accidental collapse.
Floors may not take the weight of debris or machines: get expert advice first.
An empty building can still have live services: isolate or mark them first.
Collapse isn't the only risk: dust, noise and vibration need controlling too.

sources.doc: HSE HSG150 Health and safety in construction
HSE L153 Managing health and safety in construction
